title: Towards Scalable Quantum Unit Commitment in Power Systems: Encoding and Complexity Reduction Techniques
authors: Marc Carrillo-MuÑoz, Sergio MartÍnez-Hermida, Sara Barja-MartÍnez, Antonio E. SaldaÑa GonzÁlez, MÒnica AragÜÉs-PeÑalba
abstract: This paper develops a Quantum optimisation Unit Commitment (UC) framework that benefits from Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) as a qubit reduction preprocessing technique and Sample-based Quantum Diagonalisation (SQD) as a hybrid post-processing refinement method. The UC problem is formulated in binary form, then transformed into a QUBO problem and mapped onto an Ising representation suitable for adiabatic quantum evolution within the Qibo framework. This study analyses how PCE and SQD techniques affect qubit scalability, computational effort, feasibility, and probability of recovering the optimal solution as the number of generators increases. The results show that PCE reduces the effective size of the encoded problem, SQD improves the concentration of probability on feasible and optimal solutions, and their combined application provides the best overall behaviour in several scalable case studies, achieving more reliable solutions with lower effective computational cost than the unreduced formulation. The repository is available open source in Github (link is not yet available until work is published. summary: This paper proposes an advanced, scalable quantum optimization framework for solving the Unit Commitment problem in power grids. It integrates Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) to reduce the required number of qubits and Sample-based Quantum Diagonalisation (SQD) to refine the solution quality. The combined method significantly improves reliability and scalability compared to unreduced quantum formulations.
main_problem: Developing a scalable quantum optimization framework for the Unit Commitment (UC) problem in power systems.
main_result: The combined use of Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) for qubit reduction and Sample-based Quantum Diagonalisation (SQD) for post-processing yields the best performance, achieving high probability of finding optimal and feasible solutions with lower effective computational cost.
method: The approach involves formulating the UC problem as a QUBO/Ising Hamiltonian, applying PCE to compress the Hamiltonian to fewer qubits, and then using SQD to refine the solution sampled from the reduced quantum state.
model_or_system: The system is the Unit Commitment (UC) problem in power systems, modeled mathematically as a binary optimization problem transformed into a QUBO Hamiltonian suitable for adiabatic quantum evolution (AQE).
key_observables: Probability of recovering the optimal solution ($P_{opt}$), probability of recovering a feasible solution ($P_{feas}$), effective qubit size reduction, and total computational time.
important_parameters: Number of generators ($N$), penalty parameter ($\lambda$), and the compression factor derived from PCE.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on classical emulation of quantum processes, and the effectiveness of the combined PCE+SQD workflow is tested against direct adiabatic evolution.
figures_summary: Figures compare performance metrics (probabilities, runtime) across different workflow combinations (Direct AE, AE+SQD, PCE, PCE+SQD) as the system size ($N$) increases, demonstrating the benefits of the combined approach.
paper_structure: The paper details the classical formulation of the UC problem into a QUBO, introduces the quantum workflow involving PCE preprocessing, followed by AQE, and concluding with SQD post-processing, analyzing the performance gains at each stage.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses quantum resource limitations (qubit count) and solution quality (probability concentration) in a complex, real-world optimization problem, providing a blueprint for hybrid quantum-classical solvers.
